newsitem.title: USA: Swing-N-Slide sees broader product line.
newsitem.headline: Swing-N-Slide sees broader product line.

text.p: Swing-N-Slide Corp said Wednesday its pending acquisition of GameTime Inc will allow it to broaden its playground equipment offerings and customer base.

"The impending acquisition of GameTime Inc makes us very excited about the future," Richard Mueller, chairman, said in a statement. "The 'new' Swing-N-Slide will feature a diverse roster of products for a wide variety of customers in the playground equipment industry. We also believe the combined technologies of the two companies will enhance new product development efforts."
The previously announced GameTime acquisition is expected to close by the end of the first quarter. It will more than double the size of Swing-N-Side, company said.
Going forward, GameTime is expected to account for approximately 40 percent of the operating cash flow of the combined companies, the company said.

GameTime will be operated as an independent business unit. Its playground equipment systems, which sell for up to $150,000 each, are sold directly to schools, parks and municipalities by a network of independent representatives.

The seasonality in the overall business should moderate in 1997, he added. The consumer Swing-N-Slide business typically generates 75 percent of sales in the first two quarters of the year, while GameTime has more than 60 percent of its sales during the second and third quarters of the year.

Swing-N-Slide, which sells do-it-yourself wooden playground equipment, said it expect to expand distribution of its pre-cut swing set and climbing units kits and to increase international marketing efforts.
"In addition, our Tuff Kids line, which is targeted for churches, day-care centers and lighter use applications, will receive additional sales and marketing support," Mueller said.

Earlier, Swing-N-Slide reported fourth quarter sales of $6.3 million, up from $4.8 million a year ago. It cited higher sales of core products and a contribution from the Shape Plastics product line acquisition.

The company reported a fourth quarter net loss of $0.08 a share, compared with a loss of $0.06 a year ago. For the year, it earned $0.26 a share, including an after-tax charge of $0.31 a share related to a tender offer by GreenGrass Holdings, down from $0.67 last year.
